definitions.gloss: punctuation marks (collectively); the formal term for punctuation symbols
definitions.explanation: A formal collective term for the punctuation marks used in written Japanese — the period (。), comma (、), question mark (？), exclamation mark (！), brackets (「」『』), middle dot (・), and so on. {句読符号|くとうふごう} appears in style guides, school grammar instruction, and editorial discussion; in everyday speech, the more common term is {句読点|くとうてん}, although strictly that refers only to ， / 。 and , / 、.

examples.japanese: {句読符号|くとうふごう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{正|ただ}しく→正しい：00893_tadashii⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{文章|ぶんしょう}→文章：02957_bunshou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{句読符号|くとうふごう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{足|た}りない→足りる：01209_tariru⟧。
examples.english: This piece of writing is short on punctuation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{作文|さくぶん}→作文：02884_sakubun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{句読符号|くとうふごう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{使|つか}い{方|かた}→使い方：07797_tsukaikata⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{丁寧|ていねい}→丁寧：00896_teinei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{教|おし}えて→教える：00526_oshieru⟧⟦くれた→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。
examples.english: The teacher carefully taught us how to use punctuation marks in our compositions.

examples.japanese: ⟦{出版社|しゅっぱんしゃ}→出版社：11765_shuppansha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦スタイル→スタイル：03851_sutairu⟧⟦ガイド→ガイド：05116_gaido⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{句読符号|くとうふごう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{使|つか}い{方|かた}→使い方：07797_tsukaikata⟧や{全角|ぜんかく}・{半角|はんかく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{使|つか}い{分|わ}け→使い分け：11559_tsukaiwake⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{細|こま}かく→細かい：01245_komakai⟧⟦{定|さだ}められている→定める：10448_sadameru⟧。
examples.english: The publisher's style guide spells out in detail how to use punctuation marks and when to use full-width versus half-width characters.

notes:
{句読符号|くとうふごう} is a formal collective term for the various symbols used to punctuate written Japanese. It appears mostly in linguistics, editing, publishing, and school-grammar contexts; in casual conversation people simply say ⟦{句読点|くとうてん}→句読点：08650_kutouten⟧ (which strictly means just period and comma).

FORMS:
- ⟦{句|く}→句：02137_ku⟧ ("phrase") + {読|とう} ("reading") + ⟦{符号|ふごう}→符号：00042_fugou⟧ ("sign, code") → "phrase-reading symbols," i.e. punctuation marks

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {句読符号|くとうふごう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧: to use punctuation marks
- {句読符号|くとうふごう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧: to insert punctuation
- {句読符号|くとうふごう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{使|つか}い{方|かた}→使い方：07797_tsukaikata⟧: how to use punctuation marks
- {句読符号|くとうふごう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{種類|しゅるい}→種類：01560_shurui⟧: kinds of punctuation marks

KINDS OF PUNCTUATION INCLUDED:
- ⟦{句点|くてん}→句点：19157_kuten⟧ (。): period (full stop)
- ⟦{読点|とうてん}→読点：16992_touten⟧ (、): comma
- ⟦{疑問符|ぎもんふ}→疑問符：24302_gimonfu⟧ (？): question mark
- {感嘆符|かんたんふ} (！): exclamation mark
- かぎ⟦{括弧|かっこ}→括弧：00151_kakko⟧ (「」): standard quote brackets
- ⟦{二重|にじゅう}→二重：16893_nijuu⟧かぎ⟦{括弧|かっこ}→括弧：00151_kakko⟧ (『』): nested / book-title quote brackets
- {中点|なかてん} (・): middle dot
- ダッシュ (—) / ⟦リーダー→リーダー：24312_riidaa⟧ (……): dash / ellipsis

SIMILAR / CONTRASTING TERMS:
- ⟦{句読点|くとうてん}→句読点：08650_kutouten⟧: punctuation (the most common everyday term; strictly refers only to 。 and 、 but often used loosely for all punctuation)
- ⟦{符号|ふごう}→符号：00042_fugou⟧: symbol, code, sign (the broader noun)
- ⟦{記号|きごう}→記号：00224_kigou⟧: symbol, mark (an even broader category, including math and music symbols)

USAGE:
- In daily speech and basic school instruction, ⟦{句読点|くとうてん}→句読点：08650_kutouten⟧ is by far the more common term. {句読符号|くとうふごう} is used when speakers want to be clear that the full set of punctuation symbols is meant, not just commas and periods.
- Most ordinary Japanese readers will recognize {句読符号|くとうふごう} but rarely use it actively; encountering it usually signals a formal, technical, or editorial context.
